extracted.intended_audience: students and instructors of combinatorics (advanced undergraduate / graduate)
extracted.subtask_description: The page provides the textbook's rubric for rating exercises by difficulty (levels 1–5), with additional gradations (+/−) and an asterisk convention; intended to guide assignment and reader expectations. It explains what each numeric rating means and gives interpretive guidance for borderline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty level 1
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rating 1 denotes exercises that are routine and straightforward. Further gradations like [1–] denote an utterly trivial problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty level 2
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rating 2 indicates somewhat difficult or tricky problems. A notation like [2+] denotes about the hardest problem that could be reasonably assigned to a class of graduate students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty level 3
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rating 3 denotes difficult problems. The text notes that a few students may be capable of solving a [3–] problem, while almost none could solve a [3] in a reasonable period of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty level 4
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rating 4 labels problems as horrendously difficult; these are well beyond routine graduate assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty level 5
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rating 5 denotes unsolved problems. A further gradation [5–] can indicate an unsolved problem that has received little attention and may not be too difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plus/minus gradations
rubrics_metrics.description: Further gradations are indicated by + and −.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The + and − modifiers refine a numeric rating (e.g., [2+] is slightly harder than 2, [1–] is easier than 1). Examples: [1–] denotes an utterly trivial problem; [5–] denotes an unsolved problem that has received little attention and may not be too difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk convention
rubrics_metrics.description: An asterisk after the difficulty rating indicates that no solution is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an exercise bears an asterisk (e.g., [2]*), it signals that the textbook does not provide a solution to that problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjectivity and caveats about ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: The ratings are subjective and context-dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors note the ratings are subjective and that when problems require techniques from other branches of mathematics (not usually associated with combinatorics), the rating is less meaningful. Thus the assignment of a rating reflects expected difficulty for the intended readership but may vary with background and cleverness.
